record.headline: P.E.I. firefighter, 20 years in, now teaches others about PTSD
record.summary: CBC reports on a firefighter from Prince Edward Island who served about 20 years before something gave way. He now teaches others about post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD).
record.why_it_matters: Firefighters and other first responders often carry the job home, and hearing from someone who has been through it can make asking for help feel less like a risk.
record.take: We like what we can see here: someone who lived it is now the one teaching it. Peer voices carry weight in a firehouse in ways a pamphlet never will. Mental health support for first responders should be easy to reach and free of stigma, and stories like this help push that along.
record.x_post: A P.E.I. firefighter spent 20 years on the job, hit a breaking point, and now teaches others about PTSD. Peer voices matter in the fire service. We're watching for more detail on his work. via CBC
record.fb_post:
CBC is reporting on a Prince Edward Island firefighter who spent 20 years on the job before something gave way. He now teaches others about PTSD.

Why it matters: first responders often carry the calls with them long after the shift ends. When someone from your own ranks speaks up, it can make reaching out feel a lot less like a career risk.

Our view: peer-led education is one of the best tools we have for cutting stigma. Help should be easy to find and easy to ask for.

We only have the headline and a short snippet so far, so we don't know the details of his program yet. Have you seen peer-led mental health training work in your department or unit?
